provenance.title: [Refactor] Reduce coupling in the 199 highly coupled files flagged by CodeFlow
provenance.method: git archive <commit> | tar -x -C /tmp/src && node run-analysis.mjs /tmp/src <codeflow-ui> /tmp/out; the delivered tree is snapshotted the same way from `git ls-files --cached --others --exclude-standard` because a branch has no commit id until the pipeline commits it
provenance.metric: architectureIssues["N Highly Coupled"] — analyzed files whose incoming connections exceed 8 (`coupling[conn.target] > 8` over `data.connections`, heuristic-regex mode). NOT an import count, and not a per-file import list.
provenance.premiseNote: The filing reads the metric as 'files that import 8+ other files' and prescribes splitting them. Splitting moves edges to the new file instead of deleting them, and the measured history says so: #2003 moved 101 → 116 and #2004 116 → 120. `data.connections` entries are `{source, target, fn}` — `source` defines `fn`, `target` references it — and a name with a single definition repo-wide is resolved without consulting imports, so prose and quoted examples create edges too.
provenance.filedVsMeasured: 163 files are flagged on the measured base commit, not 199: main advanced past analyzedAt and #2002/#2003/#2005 already removed phantoms. Acceptance is the measured drop on the delivered tree, as in #2002 and #2033.

after.commitNote: The pipeline commits after this record is written, so the delivered tree is stamped by `reducedFilesDigest` instead: sha1 over the sorted `reducedBy` paths, each followed by the sha1 of its content. Recomputing it from the branch reproduces the measurement.

reducedBy.edit: two comment blocks and one inline comment describe the repository-root and git-runner seams instead of naming the two declarations; both names are single definitions repo-wide, so every comment that spelled them was an edge
the file header and the import-audit phase note say `assertion` / `check` and `among them`; `guard` resolves to the Rust `sessions_store.rs` declaration and `list` to `sessions_store.rs`
the Bug #643 note says `next phase` instead of `next stage`; `stage` resolves to the Go test helper in `dockerfile_stage_split_test.go`
the `IssueFact` doc comments say `one report` and `carries no description`; `parse` resolves to `controls.rs` and `none` to `auth.rs`
the `runInitLegacyAuth` doc comment names the init orchestrator instead of the function; `runInit` is the only way the two live in one sentence
two log messages and one comment say `without blocking` / `Non-blocking` instead of `fail-open`; `open` is a single declaration in `ws.rs`

the record accessor is `allRecords` (not `all`) and its three doc lines say `every`/`the records`; the only `all` declaration in the tree — two getters — is gone, which also unflags the two Rust readers that mentioned the word

deferred.reason: 177 of the 322 remaining edges into a target that never executes the name come from declarations in Rust sources (`sessions_store.rs` `dir`/`list`/`guard`, `ws.rs` `open`/`keep`, `controls/tests.rs` `failed`, `extension_ui.rs` `timeout`, `main.rs` `root`)
deferred.requires: a lane with cargo (cargo build + cargo test) — none is installed in this image, so a rename there would be an unverified guess

deferred.reason: port contracts stay flagged: `config.go Path()`, `rpc/framing.rs fn clone`, `proper-lockfile-ambient.ts` `lock`/`check`, `helpers_run_test.go Run()`/`CombinedOutput()` are the interface, not a naming accident
deferred.requires: a detector that understands interface methods, or an accepted API break

deferred.reason: 80 remaining `.ts` edges name real domain words in exported APIs (`timeout`, `check`, `cleanup`, `install`, `supervisor`, `runAgentLoop`) — removing them means renaming exported surface and every caller, for one unflagged file each
deferred.requires: a dedicated rename batch accepted as an API change

deferred.reason: test-only `.mts` files are never scored (`Parser.codeExts` has no `.mts`), so phantoms there move nothing and none is claimed as a reduction
deferred.requires: nothing; recorded so a later re-measure does not chase them

deferred.reason: the seam that pruned non-dependency edges upstream of the report is gone, not dormant: the pinned analyzer derives `N Highly Coupled` inline inside `Parser.analyze` (index.html:5382) and exposes no deriver to re-title it, so a prune could not be reflected in the exported card. Pruning it anyway would also have under-counted real dependencies — the stripper read a template interpolation as text, a Rust `'a` lifetime or `char` literal as a string, and a Go raw string or Python triple-quoted docstring as one blob
deferred.requires: an analyzer ref that exposes an architecture deriver, or a language-aware (tree-sitter) edge predicate upstream
